## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

The *Kodhapariññā Sutta* ("Complete Understanding of Anger", Iti 12) is a discourse preserved in the *Ekakanipāta* of the *Itivuttaka*. The core teaching of the sutta states that when the mind is cleansed of passion for anger (*kodha*) and abandons it, one is capable of bringing an end to suffering.

 Computational analysis through DharmaNexus highlights extensive Pali-internal text reuse, recording 39 matching passages shared across 12 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The strongest structural and formulaic agreements occur with sibling discourses in the *Itivuttaka* that treat the understanding and renunciation of other unwholesome states, notably the *Mohapariññā Sutta* (Iti 11), *Makkhapariññā Sutta* (Iti 13), *Sabbapariññā Sutta* (Iti 7), *Dosapariññā Sutta* (Iti 10), and *Lobhapariññā Sutta* (Iti 9), alongside the *Dosa Sutta* (Iti 2) and *Moha Sutta* (Iti 3) [DharmaNexus]. In addition, DharmaNexus identifies significant formulaic overlap with portions of the *Saḷāyatana Saṁyutta* (SN 35) [DharmaNexus].
